claims.statement: The lcchess console script maps to langchain_chess_cli.main:app, a Typer app with uci, play and grade subcommands; the CLI requires Python >=3.13 and offers an optional anthropic extra.

The CLI is installed without cloning via uv from the git subdirectory libs/cli (uvx or uv tool install) because the packages are not on PyPI and uv resolves sibling packages from the same commit; an installed lcchess doesn't read .env, and calling Anthropic directly with a bare model name needs the anthropic extra plus LANGSMITH_GATEWAY unset.
mise run dev:tui runs `uv run --all-packages --env-file .env lcchess play`, with extra play options passed after `--`.

play and uci expose one flag per ChessContext setting, built by _setting from the field's description and default; every flag defaults to None so an omitted flag keeps the base settings' value, and defaults come from ChessContext (policy hybrid, model langsmith:baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash, reasoning_effort unset, model_kwargs {}, show_fen/show_board on, move_list both, memory off, systemone_model semif-qwen3.5-4b, threshold 0.9, k 5, gate margin, style rich, seed 0); play additionally takes --side and --draw-claims.

The CLI uses the shared langchain_chess_systemone.agent.build_agent, which adds SystemOneMiddleware for every policy except llm; for policy systemone it never calls the model factory and configures System 1 with threshold and tournament_threshold 0.0 and has_model=False, so System 1 always plays.

build_agent enables memory only when settings.memory is set and a model exists (so it is dropped for policy systemone); with memory on and a model whose input_limit is None it raises ChessContractError saying the model has no known input limit, so it can't use memory.

The default model is chat_model(settings.model, arguments(settings)), with model_kwargs merged over reasoning_effort; chat_model sets an output budget of MAX_TOKENS 64000 capped by the model's output limit and half of a smaller window, names the span after the bare model name, sends a reasoning effort only when set, and gives langsmith: gateway models with a known window a profile with max_input_tokens = window minus the budget.

run_config(surface, thread_id, settings) sets configurable.thread_id, run_name chess-<surface>, tags [surface], and metadata with the surface, every settings key from dump(settings) (including version and draw_claims), overlaid by sent(settings) so reasoning_effort (and max_tokens when set) record the values actually sent after model_kwargs; both the TUI (surface tui) and UCI engine (surface uci) use it.

lcchess play builds the agent through a factory taking a checkpointer that calls build_agent(settings, checkpointer=...), so draw claims follow settings.draw_claims (default auto); ChessApp creates its own InMemorySaver and calls the factory once in its constructor, so TUI games are not persisted beyond the process and build errors surface before the TUI opens; uci forces draw_claims never.
ChessApp binds ctrl+n (new game), ctrl+f (new game on the other side), ctrl+s (start), ctrl+r (retry) and ctrl+q (quit).

The TUI derives the board by replaying the thread's moves from start_fen (board_of) and renders status, details, move list and header subtitle via pure view functions over the thread state; the subtitle from describe_settings takes the effort from sent(settings), so it reflects a reasoning_effort given in model_kwargs, and adds the suffix only when an effort is set.

Moves can be entered by clicking a piece then a target, by arrow keys plus Enter/Space on the board, or by typing SAN/UCI into the input; printable non-space keys pressed on the board are forwarded to the input via a Typed message, and board moves arrive as Moved(uci) messages that go through the same _play path.
The TUI does not validate notation itself: typed text is sent as a human message and invalid input is reported through the thread state's error field shown under the status.

The board widget only accepts selection when interactive (otherwise it rings the bell), clears the selection when the position changes or it becomes non-interactive, and opens a PromotionScreen for promotions where the chosen letter is appended to the UCI and cancel posts nothing.

Board geometry picks the largest square height that fits with square width 2*h+1, supports both orientations for drawing and click hit-testing, and square colours are chess-board--<role> component classes restylable by CSS with a fixed highlight priority (selected, cursor, check, capture, last move, plain).

Each agent run is a Textual worker in the agent-run group streaming astream with stream modes messages and values on the thread captured at submit: values chunks replace the app state, model-node message text accumulates in the Analysis pane, and afterwards (even on an ordinary exception) the state is reloaded via aget_state and running is cleared; an exception records the failure while the turn stays pending.

Start sends a human go message only when nothing is running or pending, no moves exist and it is the agent's turn, and is triggered automatically for a new game as Black; retry sends an empty payload on the same thread only when a turn is pending and nothing is running, so a retried turn commits once.
Human moves are rejected with a warning while the agent runs, a turn is pending, the game is over, or it is not the human's turn; the board is interactive only when all these conditions allow a move.

A new game cancels the agent-run worker group, starts a _forget worker that waits for the cancelled runs to unwind and then deletes the previous thread's checkpoints with adelete_thread, and creates a new tui-<uuid> thread with reset state; late events and failures from the previous game therefore never reach the new game.

TUI visual regressions are SVG snapshot tests (board sizes, selection, Black orientation, promotion dialog, and a full game screen built with ChessContext(policy=llm) and a latency clock patched to zero) updated with pytest --snapshot-update after inspecting the SVGs.
The TUI's status, details, moves and analysis widgets are Static with markup disabled, so model output, errors and SAN are displayed literally rather than parsed as Rich markup.

The CLI resolves settings from an optional --config versioned settings file (or ChessContext() defaults), then overlay resets each --reset key to its default and applies the given flags before revalidating; unknown reset keys or version raise SettingsError, and any ValueError (bad file, bad --model-kwargs JSON, invalid value) becomes typer.BadParameter with exit code 2.
